summary: Revise at 5.6. Caiman scores 7 and the ship bar is 7.5. Every recorded gate is green and matches report.json. The template gate has not been run yet, so it is not counted. The identity now holds: at 300 px the sprig of two spined leaves with a three-berry bunch where the stems meet says holly with no caption. The execution is well below the bar. (1) The 18-leaf bench-cut 'Wreath' frame round the table was not in the plan. It renders as a torn, dashed border of stepped chips that boxes the sprig in and reads as damage, not leaves. (2) Every stamp is a flat, vertical-walled extrusion. The leaf margins and the vein comb show stair-steps in stones.png. The 0.4 mm face leaves (planned at 0.55; the read-test asked for 0.9) give almost no modelling, and the gable leaves the lower half of each leaf lost in the field. (3) The cheek berries stand in straight rows of three on metal cones on the head end walls. They read as rivets on stalks, and the cones show above and below the table in face.png. Each cheek carries two leaves, not the planned three. (4) The shoulder garland is four isolated flat leaves a side, about 28 deg apart. In reverse.png they read as bat silhouettes stuck on a plain shank, not a garland. Density and the large/medium/small hierarchy are far below Caiman and the Reptilia sheet: most of the ring is bare polished stock. None of read-test 2's three changes was carried out (leaf 6.3 mm, not 7.5; height 0.4, not 0.9; no field separation). A concrete round can lift this, and two rounds remain.
strengths: The plant reads at 300 px without the caption. Two spined holly leaves end to end on the parting line with a tight triangle of three garnet berries at their junction is the classic holly sprig. The attempt-1 'face with eyes' is gone.
The garnet tint is a good berry red, and the face berries sit low and flush with 0.27 mm between girdles: a real bunch.

The face leaves and the shoulder garland are struck on the parting line with parting_monotone true on all 10 cast stamps. The sand doctrine is respected, and every gate is green at draft, coarse and export.
The factory 006 table keeps its hard wall-to-face angles and crisp end walls (bare-vs-finished.png).
Theme discipline is right in intent: holly only, face to palm, and no foreign motifs.

checklist.item: One theme face to palm, nothing scattered
checklist.reason: Holly only, but scattered. The table's wreath frame breaks into 18 separate chips with gaps. The cheek berries are rows of beads on cones. The shoulder garland is four lone leaves a side with 3+ mm of bare shank between them (reverse.png, shoulder.png). Nothing connects the parts into a growing plant: no stem or vine runs the garland.

checklist.item: Reads as its plant at 300 px without the caption
checklist.reason: hero-300 and face-300 both read as holly: spined leaves plus a red berry bunch. The weakness is that it reads as 'a signet with a holly badge', not a holly ring.

checklist.item: Figurative motifs have true outlines, crisp, no combing/smearing/stair-steps
checklist.reason: These are true-outline stamps, but stones.png shows stair-stepped walls on the wreath chips and on the face-leaf spines and bays. The vein comb's chevrons are jagged, and the right face leaf's lower margin is ragged. The garland leaves in reverse.png have stepped edges.

checklist.item: Stones in made settings, visible, coloured as fruit
checklist.reason: The face berries pass: flush gypsy mounds, berry red, a true bunch. The cheek berries fail: each is a straight line of three on a tall conical stalk on the head end wall (side.png, palm.png). They read as rivets or mushrooms, not a berry cluster, and the cones show as spikes above and below the table in face.png.

checklist.item: No flat, blocky or mechanical CAD; forms sculpted
checklist.reason: Every leaf is a constant-height extrusion with vertical walls. The face leaves are 0.4 mm with a single gable crease. The garland and cheek leaves are flat plates. Nothing cups, curls or overlaps the way a holly leaf does.

checklist.item: Factory stock keeps its hard wall-to-face angles
checklist.reason: Table edges and end walls stay sharp, matching the bare stock in bare-vs-finished.png.

checklist.item: Silhouette distinct from other Vepres rings
checklist.reason: Ilex is the first Vepres ring built, and the square 006 signet is unique in the plan. The finished relief barely breaks the stock outline, though: the silhouette is the bare stock's.

checklist.item: Large, medium and small forms; density and legibility at least Caiman's
checklist.reason: Large: the bare signet. Medium: two face leaves and the berry bunch, covering about 30% of the table. Small: sparse chips and veins. The shank, cheek walls and palm are mostly bare polished metal, far sparser than Caiman's fully worked table and walls or the Reptilia sheet.

Face leaf 1-2 and Garland leaf left/right 1-4 all true at draft and export. Cheek leaves are along_pull, off the line; wreath and veins are bench cuts

No template or verification record in report.json or the folder. design.ring.json is 653,275 bytes (format 6), under the 1 MB stock budget. Not yet run, so not counted this round; it must be recorded before ship

punch_list.zone: Face table, stamps 'Wreath leaf, 1'-'Wreath leaf, 20' (theta about 65-115 deg, v about 2-18 mm)
punch_list.change: Delete the 18-chip wreath frame. In its place, give the table field a tier-1 bench matte or fine stipple, inset 0.8 mm from the table edge, so the polished sprig separates from the field. If a frame is wanted, it must be one continuous bench-cut holly-leaf border with leaves overlapping tip to stem and no gaps, not separate chips.
punch_list.acceptance: face.png and stones.png: no broken or dashed border; the sprig's outline stands out against a matte field without relying on the berries; no stair-stepped chips anywhere on the table.

punch_list.zone: Face leaves 'Face leaf, 1' / 'Face leaf, 2' (theta 73.8 / 106.2 deg, on crest_at)
punch_list.change: Carry out read-test 2's change 1, which was not done. Grow each leaf from 6.3 mm to 7.5 x 5.5 mm, tips within 0.7 mm of the head ends. Raise height_mm from 0.4 to 0.8 and the gable rise from 0.25 to 0.45. Deepen the bench midrib from 0.1 to 0.25 mm with a rounded section, and cut the side veins as separate 0.12 mm strokes, not a comb. Keep parting_monotone true.
punch_list.acceptance: hero-300: the pair spans about 15 of the 17 mm table and each leaf shows a lit midrib ridge and a dark spined margin. face.png: the lower half of each leaf is as legible as the upper half. report.json: parting_monotone true for both.

punch_list.zone: All stamp outlines (face, cheek, garland leaves and vein cuts)
punch_list.change: Remove the stair-steps. Sample each leaf outline at least 512 points with smooth spine arcs, and raise the stamp raster/chart resolution under the stamps (or build stamps as true geometry) so the walls are continuous. Give the walls a 0.1 mm top-edge round so the leaves read as cast metal, not laser-cut plate.
punch_list.acceptance: stones.png at full resolution: no visible stair-step or zig-zag on any leaf margin, spine or vein; spine tips are clean points.

punch_list.zone: Cheek sprays on the head end walls ('Cheek berry 1/2, 1-3' at theta 80.3/90/99.7, v 2.2-2.4 and 17.3-17.6; 'Cheek leaf 1/2, 1-2' at theta 61.7/118.3)
punch_list.change: Regroup each cheek's three berries from a straight row into a touching triangle (0.2-0.4 mm apart). Seat them flush in gypsy mounds no more than 0.5 mm proud of the wall: no visible cone or stalk. Add the planned third leaf per cheek, and enlarge the cheek leaves from 5.0 x 2.6 to 6.0 x 3.2 mm, splayed round the bunch at about 120 deg intervals.
punch_list.acceptance: side.png: each end wall shows a berry bunch framed by three spiny leaves. face.png and palm.png: no metal cones visible above or below the table, and berries read as fruit, not rivets.

punch_list.zone: Shoulder garland 'Garland leaf, left/right 1-4' (theta 36.4 to -48.0 and 143.6 to 228.0 on RowPath::PartingLine)
punch_list.change: Make it a garland. Raise count from 4 to 7 a side with spacing about 0.8 x leaf length so the leaves overlap tip over stem. Keep the 0.24 taper and fold_clear 1.0. Add a 0.9 mm twisted stem sweep (cad::twist) on the parting line under the leaves from the head to theta -48/228. Add pairs of 1.0 mm cast berry dots on the line at every second station if DFM allows, or bench-drilled ones if not. Give each garland leaf a Gable top (rise 0.2) so it reads as a curved blade.
punch_list.acceptance: reverse.png and shoulder.png: one continuous leafy vine runs down each shoulder with no bare gap over 1.5 mm between leaves and nothing reads as bat silhouettes. parting_monotone true on every struck garland stamp; DFM 0.

punch_list.zone: Shank flanks between garland and palm (theta about -60 to 30 and 150 to 240)
punch_list.change: Lift density to Caiman's. Add a bench-only holly-bark texture or fine stipple on the shank flanks that fades out 3 mm before the bare palm, so the palm stays bare as the plan says. Check whether the visible banding on the shank (reverse.png, shoulder.png) comes from the stock mesh or the render, and smooth it at export.
punch_list.acceptance: hero.png and reverse.png: the flanks carry small-scale texture, the shank shows no banding or stair facets, and the palm stays bare, polished metal.

punch_list.change: Run the template lift and record it: cold evaluation byte-identical, at most 4 design.set patches, size and open time in verification.json.
punch_list.acceptance: verification.json records patches <= 4, a byte-identical cold lift, and size within the stock budget (1 MB; flag over 3 MB).
